title: MultiCapsNet: A General Framework for Data Integration and Interpretable Classification.
authors: Wang, Lifei; Miao, Xuexia; Nie, Rui; Zhang, Zhang; Zhang, Jiang; Cai, Jun
one_liner_zh: 提出基于CapsNet的可解释深度学习框架MultiCapsNet，在单细胞数据中整合PPI与蛋白-DNA互作信息用于细胞类型分类，并揭示转录因子贡献，但非聚焦TF-DNA结合机制建模。
abstract: The latest progresses of experimental biology have generated a large number of data with different formats and lengths. Deep learning is an ideal tool to deal with complex datasets, but its inherent "black box" nature needs more interpretability. At the same time, traditional interpretable machine learning methods, such as linear regression or random forest, could only deal with numerical features instead of modular features often encountered in the biological field. Here, we present MultiCapsNet (https://github.com/wanglf19/MultiCapsNet), a new deep learning model built on CapsNet and scCapsNet, which possesses the merits such as easy data integration and high model interpretability. To demonstrate the ability of this model as an interpretable classifier to deal with modular inputs, we test MultiCapsNet on three datasets with different data type and application scenarios. Firstly, on the labeled variant call dataset, MultiCapsNet shows a similar classification performance with neural network model, and provides importance scores for data sources directly without an extra importance determination step required by the neural network model. The importance scores generated by these two models are highly correlated. Secondly, on single cell RNA sequence (scRNA-seq) dataset, MultiCapsNet integrates information about protein-protein interaction (PPI), and protein-DNA interaction (PDI). The classification accuracy of MultiCapsNet is comparable to the neural network and random forest model. Meanwhile, MultiCapsNet reveals how each transcription factor (TF) or PPI cluster node contributes to classification of cell type. Thirdly, we made a comparison between MultiCapsNet and SCENIC. The results show several cell type relevant TFs identified by both methods, further proving the validity and interpretability of the MultiCapsNet.
abstract_zh: 实验生物学的最新进展产生了大量不同格式和长度的数据。深度学习是处理复杂数据集的理想工具，但其固有的“黑箱”特性需要更强的可解释性。同时，传统的可解释机器学习方法，如线性回归或随机森林，只能处理数值特征，而无法处理生物学领域中常见的模块化特征。在此，我们提出了MultiCapsNet（https://github.com/wanglf19/MultiCapsNet），这是一种基于CapsNet和scCapsNet构建的新型深度学习模型，具有易于数据集成和高模型可解释性等优点。为了展示该模型作为可解释分类器处理模块化输入的能力，我们在三个具有不同数据类型和应用场景的数据集上测试了MultiCapsNet。首先，在标记的变异调用数据集上，MultiCapsNet表现出与神经网络模型相似的分类性能，并直接为数据源提供重要性评分，无需神经网络模型所需的额外重要性确定步骤。这两种模型生成的重要性评分高度相关。其次，在单细胞RNA序列（scRNA-seq）数据集上，MultiCapsNet整合了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）和蛋白质-DNA相互作用（PDI）的信息。MultiCapsNet的分类准确性与神经网络和随机森林模型相当。同时，MultiCapsNet揭示了每个转录因子（TF）或PPI簇节点如何对细胞类型分类做出贡献。第三，我们将MultiCapsNet与SCENIC进行了比较。结果显示，两种方法识别出多个与细胞类型相关的TF，进一步证明了MultiCapsNet的有效性和可解释性。
